note: Menander the most famous Indo-Greek ruler: e-PG Pathshala (INFLIBNET) 'Menander was the most famous of the Indo-Greeks (165 to 145 BCE). He was known as Milinda in Indian tradition.' Taught in s3 and people; NCERT XII also pictures his coin (Fig. 2.12).

Ashvaghosha wrote Buddhacharita: e-PG Pathshala 'Asvaghosha was the greatest literary figure of his times. In richness and variety his work viz., Buddhacharita is matchless.' Taught in s4, people and q18.
Mrichhakatikam by Shudrak: primary chapter HIS-08 (Gupta age). No fetched NCERT/INFLIBNET source for this chapter mentions Shudrak or the Mrichhakatikam, so it is not taught here.

Sakabda (Saka era) commenced 78 CE: e-PG Pathshala 'Kanishka was the founder of the Saka Era which starts from 78 CE.' NCERT XII timeline gives 'c. 78 CE? Accession of Kanishka' — the question mark is disclosed in the s1 exam_note. Taught in s4 and q04.
Nanaghat inscription describes Satakarni I: e-PG Pathshala 'the Naneghat inscription of Naganika throw much light on the achievements of the king Satakarni-I.' Taught in s5, people and q20.

Kanishka's capital Purushapura (Purushpur): e-PG Pathshala 'His capital was Purushapura (modern Peshawar).' Taught in s4 with an exam_note separating it from Mathura, the second capital (NCERT VI). q05, q37.

Thiruvalluvar and the Tirukkural's 1,330 couplets: none of the fetched authorised sources (NCERT VI/VIII/XII chapters, INFLIBNET e-PG modules on the post-Mauryan period and on Tolkappiyam/Sangam literature) states the Tirukkural's authorship or couplet count. The gap is disclosed to students in the s6 exam_note; the fact is not taught as claim-backed content.

Agathocles' coins bearing Krishna and Balarama: the fetched sources establish only the general facts that Indo-Greek coins first bore rulers' names and images (NCERT XII) and that Agathocles extended Bactrian rule south of the Hindu Kush (INFLIBNET). No fetched source mentions his Krishna-Balarama coins, so this specific item is not taught.

'Vindhya Adhipati' (Lord of the Vindhyas) = Gautamiputra Satakarni: the king himself is fully taught in s5 (greatest Satavahana, victor over Nahapana, Nasik inscription of Gautami Balashri), but the specific epithet 'Vindhya Adhipati' does not appear in any fetched NCERT/INFLIBNET text, so the epithet itself is not taught. The s5 exam_focus flags the PYQ for students.
Saka Era counting starts 78 AD: same claim as WBCS-2021-Q125 (e-PG Pathshala, Kanishka founder of the Saka era, 78 CE). Taught in s4 and q04.
